extraFacts.fact: ASME B1.20.1 is the standard for NPT tapered pipe threads, which seal on the thread with sealant.

faqs.q: What are the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees used for?
faqs.a: The Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees are brass push-to-connect male branch tees for transportation air systems, with a male NPT thread on the branch and push-in ends on the run. The listing gives the applications as heavy duty truck, trailer and mobile equipment: air brakes, air tanks, air ride, sliders, tire inflation, primary and secondary air lines and cab controls.

faqs.q: How do I read part numbers such as 172PMTNS-8-6 on the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees?
faqs.a: The three part numbers are 172PMTNS-8-6, 172PMTNS-6-6 and 172PMTNS-6-4, so the 172PMTNS series code is followed by two size codes. The rows list 3/8 NPT with an outside diameter of 1 1/2 inch for -8-6 and 1 3/8 inch for -6-6 and -6-4. Quote the full number.

faqs.q: What sizes do the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees come in?
faqs.a: The Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees list 3 part numbers: 172PMTNS-8-6, 172PMTNS-6-6 and 172PMTNS-6-4. The rows state the body outside diameter, 1 1/2 inch on -8-6 and 1 3/8 inch on the other two, and 3/8 NPT on the two rows that give a thread. The size table gives the connection of each row.

faqs.q: What pressure are the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees rated for?
faqs.a: The rows state a pressure of 0 psi to 250 psi for the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees, and 172PMTNS-6-4 says up to 250 psi. The tube you push in may be rated lower than the fitting, so use the lower of the two ratings. The listing gives no temperature range, so ask us to confirm it for your climate.

faqs.q: What are the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees made of?
faqs.a: The Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees are brass, as the listing states, in the Prestomatic series. The listing does not give the seal material, collet material or any plating, so ask us to confirm them for the exact part number, such as 172PMTNS-6-6, if the fitting runs on a vehicle in a harsh environment.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees?
faqs.a: The listing names no standard or certificate for the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees and describes them as a push-to-connect transportation fitting. If your brake or air system specification calls for a standard, state it on the RFQ with a part number such as 172PMTNS-8-6 and we confirm what the maker supplies.

faqs.q: What tube and thread do the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees connect to?
faqs.a: The branch has a male 3/8 NPT thread, which screws into a female NPT port, and the run takes the push-in tube. The listing does not state the tube material, so check the tube against the [pneumatic tubing materials guide](/blog/pneumatic-tubing-materials-guide). More push-in parts are in the [push-to-connect pneumatic fittings range](/c/push-to-connect-pneumatic-fittings).

faqs.q: How do I install the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees?
faqs.a: Seal the male NPT thread as the [guide to stopping an NPT leak](/blog/stopping-an-npt-thread-leak) describes, tighten the branch into the port, then cut the tube square and push it fully home into the push-in ends. Check the tube is held by pulling gently on it. The [guide to push-to-connect air fittings](/blog/push-to-connect-air-fittings) covers the connect and release steps.

faqs.q: Where are the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees used?
faqs.a: The listing gives the applications as heavy duty truck, trailer and mobile equipment: air brakes, air tanks, air ride, sliders, tire inflation, primary and secondary air lines and cab controls. Tell us the vehicle system, the tube and the port thread and we confirm the Parker Prestomatic 172PMTNS Male Branch Tees suit it. They are for the compressed air side of the vehicle, not for hydraulic or fuel lines.
